The fog had swallowed half the stairs. Serin braced her left hand on the railing. The iron was cold enough to stick to her palm.

"Anyone up here?"

Instead of an answer, the bell upstairs shivered once. It did not ring. Serin held her breath and counted her own steps.

In front of the dock warehouse Serin made a fist. Old Gwak's laughter rolled in through the fog. It kept turning her mother's story into something cheap.

"You just made that up."

Serin swallowed a mouthful of cold air and turned away. The wind from the tower carried the smell of iron.

In the market alley Serin slowed down. Warden Baek's voice came from a shop behind her. Courteous, with a smooth curl at the end.

"Young miss, out early."

Serin did not answer. She only tightened her left hand around the Silver Key. Even at midday the smell of fog would not lift.

On the stone steps before the tower Do Yunseo stopped. He looked at the far fog and said little.

"Go back for today."

Serin took one step back. There was no explanation in it, and the night air sank cold around them.

Do Yunseo did not look at the letter's seal. To her question he turned his face away instead of answering.

"Don't ask."

Serin asked nothing more. Far off came the sound of the bell trembling without ringing. He closed his eyes for a moment, as if he knew that sound.

Before opening the chest, Serin remembered her mother's note. Short, tidy letters. Han Seoyeon always wrote like that.

"Am I not allowed to say I miss you?"

Serin murmured it alone and shut the lid. The room was cold, and the fog lay low outside the window.

In the orphanage kitchen Yun Haeok held out a bowl of soup. The steam warmed the tip of Serin's nose.

"Eat first. Talk later."

Serin wrapped the bowl in both hands. Her fingers, frozen all day, loosened little by little. Far off came the sound of the market closing.

On the foggy docks Serin stood facing Do Yunseo.

"Why didn't you tell me? You knew all of it."

"Knowing is not everything."

A cold wind slipped between them. Far off, a boat's bell rang short.

Serin traced the thin scratch on the Silver Key with her nail. The fine line caught the moonlight.

"I'll go all the way."

The wind came from the tower. Even in the fog the tower's outline stood clear. Serin let go of the railing and took one step.

Serin crouched beneath the orphanage stairs. She was ashamed to be late when the Director called.

"Sorry. I'm late."

Yun Haeok did not scold her, only said her name. The cold air of the corridor touched her cheek. Serin stood up without lifting her head.
